author: ValWood
body:
Although maybe it is processing (sorry)!

https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0014482707003953?via%3Dihub
Discussion
The OPA1 protein exists as multiple isoforms resulting from alternate splicing and proteolytic cleavage of sequences situated upstream of the GTPase domain. Two major l-forms, proposed to have a mitochondrial pro-fusion activity, can be cleaved in 3 s-forms that are suggested to have a mitochondrial pro-fission and anti-apoptotic activities. To gain insights in the regulatory mechanisms controlling this crucial proteolytic step, we have reconsidered which stimuli governs OPA1 cleavage.

I can't figure out if it is cleaved to inactivate/remove one isoform,  or the cleaved version is the active version. It all seems a bit vague.

Apparently the same situation in cerevisiae

From the same paper, this is the yeast background
Initially characterized in S. cerevisiae, the proteolytic cleavage of MGM1 by Rbd1/Pcp1, an IM embedded rhomboid-like serine protease, generates a short (s) form from a long (l) form [[14]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0014482707003953?via%3Dihub#bib14). In yeast, this cleavage is ATP-dependent and acts on the mitochondrial morphology and DNA maintenance [[14]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0014482707003953?via%3Dihub#bib14). A similar OPA1 proteolytic cleavage process generating 3 s-forms from 2 l-forms has recently been described although in somewhat controversial terms. On one hand, OPA1 could be cleaved by the presenilin-associated rhomboid-like protease (PARL), orthologous of Pcp1 in yeast, to control the apoptotic process independently of the mitochondrial fusion–fission activities [[15]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0014482707003953?via%3Dihub#bib15). On the other hand, OPA1 could be cleaved by the m-AAA Paraplegin and AFG3L2 proteases to control mitochondrial fusion in a ΔΨm-dependent manner [[16]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0014482707003953?via%3Dihub#bib16), [[17]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0014482707003953?via%3Dihub#bib17). In fact, both processes are compatible with the existence of multiple cleavages sites in the amino-terminus region of OPA1 and with OPA1 functional dichotomy [[4]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0014482707003953?via%3Dihub#bib4). The relevance of OPA1 cleavage has been further highlighted by its identification in cells with mutation in the nuclear tfam and polγ genes or in the mitochondrial tRNAlys gene that compromise the mitochondrial energetic status [[18]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0014482707003953?via%3Dihub#bib18). In these cells, the mitochondrial network is systematically fractionated and shows increased cleavage of OPA1 isoforms, as in cells treated with CCCP that dissipates the ΔΨm. This suggests that a tight correlation exists between the dissipation of the ΔΨm, the fission of the mitochondrial network and the cleavage of OPA1 [[18]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0014482707003953?via%3Dihub#bib18). But because apoptosis, mitochondrial fission and ΔΨm dissipation are intimately intricate mechanisms, with many downstream consequences on mitochondrial activities and physical properties, it remains unclear which is the central mechanism governing OPA1 cleavage.
